newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: After 100 days, Hasina sees prosperity ahead.
newsitem.headline: After 100 days, Hasina sees prosperity ahead.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday her 100-day-old government was firmly committed to lead the impoverished country to prosperity.
"I can assure you that Bangladesh will emerge as an economic tiger in the near future," she told a live question-and-answer session on Bangladesh television on Tuesday night.
"We are taking bold steps to free the country from illegal arms and restore law and order. We are trying to boost agricuture, quicken industrialisation and attract investment.
"We have received commitments of over $1 billion worth of foreign direct investment and have set a target for achieving seven percent growth of GDP (Gross Domestic Product) over the next one year.
"My government is earnestly pursuing a goal to make our country Golden Bangladesh," the prime minister said. "Our first 100 days in power has been a story of success."
The prime minister referred to a chronic power shortage that slowed industrial production and discouraged investors. "We are trying to get enough supply of electricity at the shortest possible time.

"If needed, we will buy electricity, no matter who feels what about it," she said about the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)'s threat to scuttle plans to import power from neighbouring India.
Hasina said she expected a deal with India before the next dry seaon (December) for sharing water from the Ganges river.
Dhaka officials say the Ganges is vital for irrigation, navigation and ecological balance in northern Bangladesh, where some 40 million people are facing gradual desertification.
The prime minister said she had asked police to arrest anyone involved in "terrorism" irrespective of political affiliation.
Hasina said police arrested 867 people for possessing illegal firearms and seized 1,167 weapons since she took office on June 23 after elections returned her Awami League to power.
